'''Signe Helene Kjelstrup''' (born August 29, 1949) is a Norwegian professor of [[physical chemistry]] at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU) in [[Trondheim]], Norway. She is a [[principal investigator]] at PoreLab, a [[Center of excellence|Center of Excellence]] at NTNU.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://porelab.no/principal-investigators-and-employees/|title=Principal Investigators – PoreLab|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-29}}</ref>

Her main area of research is [[non-equilibrium thermodynamics]], and in August 2019 PoreLab hosted «The International Workshop on Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics in Porous Media» on the occasion of professor Kjelstrup's 70th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://porelab.no/|title=PoreLab – Centre of Excellence (SFF)|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-29}}</ref>

== Education and professional career ==
Kjelstrup was born in Oslo. She has  an [[Master of Science|Msc]] ([[sivilingeniør]]) in chemistry from the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] (NTH), [[Trondheim]], (1971) and her thesis received the honour «commended to the King» (''laudabilis cum litteris commendatitiis''). This was the first time in the history of the school that a woman received this highest honour.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=N.N.|date=August 27, 2019|title=Jubilant|journal=Adresseavisen|language=no|pages=36}}</ref>

In 1974 she received the degree lic. techn.<ref>precursor to the dr.ing. degree</ref> with the thesis ''Complex formations in alkali-aluminium fluoride melts.''<ref>{{Cite book|title=Complex formations in alkali-aluminium fluoride melts.|last=Ratkje|first=Signe Helene Kjelstrup|publisher=Norges tekniske høgskole|year=1974|series=Avhandling (lic. techn.)|location=NTNU University Library, Trondheim}}</ref> She later received a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright grant]] and worked as an [[assistant professor]] at the School of Medicine and Dentistry, [[University of Rochester]] (New York, USA).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://kjemi.no/selskapet-arkiv/pdf/guldberg-waage-2014.pdf|title=Tildeling av Norsk Kjemisk Selskaps medalje til minne om Guldberg og Waages massevirkningslov til Professor Signe Kjelstrup.|last=N.N.|date=March 11, 2014|website=Kjemidigital.no|publisher=Norwegian Chemical Society|language=no|access-date=September 12, 2019}}</ref>

She has a [[Doctor of Technology|dr.techn.]] degree from 1982. Her thesis is titled ''On the energetics of coupled transport processes : a theoretical and experimental irreversible thermodynamic investigation.''<ref>{{Cite book|title=On the energetics of coupled transport processes : a theoretical and experimental irreversible thermodynamic investigation|last=Ratkje|first=Signe Kjelstrup|publisher=Norges tekniske høgskole|year=1982|isbn=82-00-23126-7|location=NTNU University Library}}</ref>

In 1985 Kjelstrup was appointed professor at NTH.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=N.N.|date=1985|title=Professor i fysikalsk kjemi|journal=Unitnytt|language=no|volume=6|pages=11}}</ref> Together with Professor [[Tormod Førland]], she developed the field of irreversible thermodynamics there.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Lykknes |first=Annette |author-link=Annette Lykknes |title=Akademi og industri : kjemiutdanning og -forskning ved NTNU gjennom 100 år |last2=Gusland |first2=Joakim Ziegler |publisher=Fagbokforlaget |year=2015 |isbn=9788245018288 |location=NTNU University Library (and others) |pages=389, 447}}</ref> Her scientific work has been of great importance in this field.<ref name=":2" /> She is particularly interested in improving the [[second law of thermodynamics]] and of [[Renewable energy|renewable energy technology]].<ref name=":1" />

She has been a visiting professor at several foreign universities: [[University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences|Medical College of Ohio]] (1988/1989); [[Leiden University]] (1997/1998); [[Kyoto University]] (2000) and [[University of Barcelona]] (2004).<ref name=":2" />

== Memberships and honours ==
Kjelstrup is an elected member of [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://english.dnva.no/c40133/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40187|title=Artikkel: Group 4: Chemistry|website=english.dnva.no|access-date=2019-08-29}}</ref>  [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntva.no/medlemmer/medlemsoversikt/|title=Medlemsoversikt|last=wpnimda|website=NTVA - Norges Tekniske Vitenskapsakademi|language=nb-NO|access-date=2019-08-29}}</ref> and [[Royal Norwegian Society of Sciences and Letters]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dknvs.no/akademiet/medlemmer/gruppe-iii-kjemi/|title=Gruppe III Kjemi {{!}} DKNVS|language=nb-NO|access-date=2019-08-29}}</ref>

She has been awarded an honorary doctorate at The [[Northeastern University (China)|Northeastern University of China]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://kjemi.no/guldberg-og-waage-medaljen/|title=Guldberg og Waage-medaljen – Norsk Kjemisk Selskap|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-29}}</ref>

She has received the Guldberg and Waage medal from the [[Norwegian Chemical Society]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1980 she received «Fridtjof Nansens belønning for yngre forskere», (the Fridtjof Nansen Reward for young scientists).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nansenfondet.no/Yngre_forskere.html|title=Styret|website=www.nansenfondet.no|language=no|access-date=2019-09-10}}</ref>

In 2018 her daughter, the composer [[Maja Ratkje]], wrote the musical work «A Highway in State Space», dedicated to Kjelstrup and inspired by her research. The work, which has the same title as one of Kjelstrup's [[Academic publishing|research articles]], was part of the project and album ''Sound of Science,'' where seven composers were invited by the musician [[Kronos Quartet|Jeffrey Zeigler]] to contribute with a new piece of music each.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ratkje.no/2018/11/the-sound-of-science-featuring-jeffrey-zeigler/|title=The Sound of Science featuring Jeffrey Zeigler {{!}} Maja Solveig Kjelstrup Ratkje|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thequietus.com/articles/25480-maja-ratkje-interview|title=The Quietus {{!}} Features {{!}} A Quietus Interview {{!}} Irresponsible Science - An Interview With Maja S. K. Ratkje|website=The Quietus|language=en-us|access-date=2019-09-10}}</ref>
